content: 1. To create a board review question, begin by thoroughly reading and understanding the material being tested. This ensures you grasp the fundamental principles, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and therapeutic interventions at the level expected for board examinations. 2. Familiarize yourself with the format, content, and high-yield material relevant to the exam. Always respect copyright laws and use legitimate sources, such as question banks, for reference. 3. Select a specific topic or content area. Utilize resources like WikiDoc to gather information, images, videos, and links that can aid in explaining the concepts. 4. Design the question to challenge the test taker. Avoid directly revealing the correct answer. Instead, describe clinical signs and symptoms in lay terms to provide subtle hints. For example, instead of stating Marfanoid appearance, describe the patient as having long extremities, a thin build, and tall stature. 5. Avoid using negative phrasing in the question stem, such as Which of the following is NOT correct? or Which of the following is false? 6. Use long question stems to simulate the complexity of real test scenarios. Short or moderate-length stems can be used to test specific facts. 7. Incorporate multi-step or jump questions to assess the test taker's medical reasoning process. For example, present a clinical vignette, followed by questions that require identifying the diagnosis, selecting the treatment of choice, explaining its mechanism of action, and recognizing the most common adverse effect of the treatment. 8. Reverse the order of steps or add additional layers of complexity to create a more challenging jump question. 9. When designing microbiology questions, ensure they require the test taker to make a diagnosis, identify the treatment of choice, and understand the mechanism of action. Avoid overly simplistic or less elegant questions, such as asking for an HLA subtype associated with a disease. 10. To upload a question on WikiDoc, navigate to the homepage and click on the Board Review icon. Then, select Add a board review question. Enter your name in the author box, choose the exam type, and select one main category and an appropriate subcategory for the question. 11. Provide an overall explanation in the designated box, focusing on the correct answer choice. Use the remaining boxes to input the question, answer choices, and explanations for each choice. If possible, include an image to enhance the question. 12. Save your work by clicking Save Page or preview it to see how the question will appear. Ensure you save the page before moving on. 13. Perform a self-quality check using the WikiDoc Board Review (WBR) quality checklist. Contact the WBR Editors-in-Chief or team members via email to review your question. 14. Congratulations. You have successfully created a high-quality board review question. 15. When designing the question stem, present it as a clinical vignette rather than an actual case. The information and illustrations should focus on the key testing points. Include significant patient history, family history, and diagnostic study results. Whenever possible, incorporate images (still or motion) to enhance the question. 16. Avoid negative phrasing in the question stem, such as except or not. 17. For answer choices, include five options: one correct answer and four distractors. Avoid using true or false as answer choices. Ensure all distractors are homogeneous, falling within the same category as the correct answer and similar in length. Avoid long correct answers, illogical options, absolute terms, or repeated words/phrases from the question stem. 18. Do not use answer choices like None of the above, All of the above, or combinations of responses. 19. Provide detailed answer explanations. Justify why the correct answer is correct by explaining the relevant positive findings and why the distractors are incorrect. Include concise, high-yield information and additional details not covered in the overall explanation. 20. In the overall explanation, ensure only one answer is the best or most appropriate. Justify the choice by explaining the pertinent positive and negative findings. Include educational objectives with one or two high-yield take-home points. 21. For answer choice explanations, provide a thorough yet concise rationale for the correct answer and why each distractor is incorrect. Add supplementary information to the correct answer explanation that was not included in the overall explanation.
